topics.label: Introduction to cancer causes and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture, introduces its focus on cancer causes, and states the learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer as clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: It explains cancer as the evolution of mutated cells whose growth also depends on a supportive microenvironment.

topics.label: Sources of cancer risk and the bad-luck debate
topics.groupedBecause: They develop a risk-balance account of cancer, connecting biological and environmental contributors with public interpretation of the bad-luck idea.

topics.label: Geographical cancer patterns and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: It uses geographical and migration patterns to show how epidemiology can help distinguish environmental influences from inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how pathogens can contribute to cancer and use Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate how infection and other conditions can combine in its development.

topics.label: Environmental agents and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: They show how environmental exposures can damage DNA or cause mutations, including through metabolic activation and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and context-dependent carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: They show that cancer development depends not only on mutational initiation but also on promotion and the biological context in which exposures act, then recap these mechanisms.

topics.label: Mutational signatures as evidence of carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: It explains how patterns of mutations in cancer genomes can provide evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: They compare evidence-generating approaches used to assess carcinogenicity and explain what each can and cannot establish.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: It closes the lecture by drawing together its conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the difficulty of assessing them, then frames exposure choices as risk–benefit decisions.
